Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: cleaner pay per hour, the extra pay for a same-day turn, the days of stock to hold, the wanted inspection score and the cleaning fee margin.
Check Cleaners, Team and Units. They hold your cleaners with their weekly hours and rate, the people the other sheets look up and the cleaning fee of each unit.
Log every clean on Turnovers: date, unit, cleaner, hours, pay and linen. A turnover is the clean and reset between two stays. The time to the next check-in and the tight-turn check fill in.
Open Cleaner Availability to see the booked and free hours of each cleaner and day, and Same-Day Turns to see the slack when a guest leaves and another arrives the same day.
Record each month of each cleaner on Cleaner Pay. Pay per turnover and per hour calculate themselves, and the pay statement prints from the row.
Keep Supply Items and Supply Stock up to date. The status, days of cover and quantity to order fill in, and the order list shows what to buy before the next check-in.
Log every purchase on Supply Purchases and every order on Supplier Orders. Share of spend, the days to delivery and the delivery check fill in by themselves.
Score each clean on Inspection Checks and write each redo on Redo Jobs. The pass check and the cost of the redo calculate themselves.
Count linen on Linen Counts, record each run on Laundry Runs and each deep clean on Deep Cleans. Unit Cleaning Tasks holds the minutes of every task of a unit.
Write found items on Lost and Found and notes from your cleaners on Cleaner Notes. Follow-ups that wait are flagged.
Use the 14 calculators for the day plan, workload, same-day turns, cleaner pay, cleaning cost, fee margin, reorder, days of cover, linen sets, laundry, budget, redo cost and the weekly rota.
Read the Cleaning and Supplies Dashboard and Charts every week: turnovers, pay, hours, inspections, redo jobs, stock and spend.
Keep every unit guest-ready and know what each one costs to keep
Maintenance ticket board with due dates
every problem has a priority, a fix-by date, days open and a check that shows overdue, due soon, waiting for parts or closed on time
tickets past their fix-by date turn red and a ready message goes to the handyperson and the host
Damage claim builder with evidence list
repair cost, extra cleaning, lost nights and the deposit give the amount to claim and the number of proof items to collect
deposit, claim and days since check-out say how much to return, how much to keep and whether the release is overdue
every claim shows the days it has waited, the unrecovered amount and the amount left to claim after the deposit
smoke alarms, gas, locks, extinguishers and sockets show the latest check of each unit with overdue and due soon alerts
repair cost, replacement cost, age, expected life and warranty give the cheaper choice and the cost per year of each
every appliance with its warranty end, age and a warning before the cover ends, so a faulty machine is claimed from the seller
each recurring service shows the next due date, the days left and the yearly cost, and the planner prices a new service for all units
Maintenance cost per night by unit
cost by unit and month divided by the nights booked shows which unit costs most to keep and which repairs keep coming back

Maintenance tickets from report to done
One row per problem reported in a unit: kind, priority, handyperson, status and cost; the fix-by date, days open, on-time check, next check-in and phone numbers fill in by themselves.
Damage claims against guests and platforms
One row per damage found after a stay: booking, guest, channel, amount claimed, deposit held and repair cost; days pending, the amount not recovered and what to claim after the deposit fill in.
Units with maintenance cost and next check-in
One row per unit: type, city, owner and listing date; tickets and cost of the last 12 months, cost per booked night, repeat issues, overdue safety checks and the next check-in fill in by themselves.
Bookings with the issues reported during the stay
One row per booking: unit, guest, channel, dates and status; the nights, the tickets reported during the stay and the damage claims on the booking fill in by themselves.
Safety checks with the next check date
One row per safety check: unit, item, result, who did it and the next check date; whether the check is the latest, the days left and overdue or due soon fill in by themselves.
Service schedule with the next due date
One row per recurring service of a unit: how often, when it was last done and the cost; the next due date, the days to it and the cost per year fill in by themselves.
Appliances with age and warranty left
One row per appliance in a unit: purchase date, warranty end date and cost; the days of warranty left, the age and the warranty and replacement checks fill in by themselves.
Repair quotes with decision and days waiting
One row per quote asked from a handyperson or supplier: work, amount and the decision; the days waiting, whether the owner must approve and the supplier and owner phones fill in by themselves.
One row per parts order for a ticket: part, quantity, price, supplier and delivery date; the order value, the unit, the handyperson and whether the part is late fill in by themselves.
Inspections with score and pass check
One row per walk-through inspection of a unit: who inspected, the score and the number of issues found; whether the unit passed your score fills in by itself.
Incidents during stays with action and close date
One row per incident during a stay: unit, kind, guest and the action taken; the days open and whether it is closed fill in by themselves.
Handyperson hours by week against capacity
One row per handyperson and week: hours worked and jobs done; the weekly capacity from the Team sheet, the spare hours and whether the week was full fill in by themselves.
Maintenance cost by unit and month
One row per unit and month: tickets, parts, labour and booked nights; the cost and the cost per booked night with a check against your target fill in by themselves.
One row per warranty claim: the appliance, the date, the amount and the result; the unit, the appliance name and the days waiting fill in by themselves.
One row per deposit taken on a direct booking: guest, check-out date, amount, release date and the part kept; the days since check-out and whether it is held, overdue or released fill in.
Recurring issues by unit and kind
One row per unit and ticket kind that comes back: the root cause and the fix; the tickets in the last 12 months, the last date and whether it is a repeat issue fill in by themselves.
One row per planned purchase for a unit: item, planned month, cost, yearly saving and reason; the months to go, the payback time and a payback check fill in by themselves.
Key and lock events with code changes
One row per lock event: unit, what happened, whether the entry code changed and who did it; the days ago and a warning when a lost key has no new code fill in by themselves.
Pest and exterior checks by unit
One row per pest or exterior check: unit, area, finding and the action taken; the days ago and whether the area is clear or needs action fill in by themselves.
Team with tickets handled and hours
The host, the co-host (a helper who handles guests for a fee), four cleaners, two handypeople and four outside contacts; tickets handled, cost and hours this month fill in by themselves.

Handyperson: new ticket at a unit
Hello {handyperson}, new ticket {ticket_id} at {unit}: {kind}. Please fix by {fix_by}.
Hello {handyperson}, urgent: a guest arrives at {unit} on {next_checkin}. Ticket {ticket_id} must be done before then.
Hello {supplier}, please send a quote for {work} at {unit}. I need it by the end of the week.
Hello {handyperson}, the part {part} for {unit} arrived. Please book the repair for ticket {ticket_id}.
Hello {handyperson}, your visit at {unit} for ticket {ticket_id} is confirmed. The guest is {guest}.
Hello {handyperson}, please add photos before and after for ticket {ticket_id} at {unit}.
Hello {handyperson}, thank you. Ticket {ticket_id} at {unit} is closed. Total cost {cost}.
Handyperson: a safety check is due
Hello {done_by}, a safety check is due at {unit}: {item}. Next check date {next_check}.
Guest: sorry, we fix it today
Hello {guest}, we are sorry about the problem at {unit}. We are fixing it today and will tell you when it is done.
Hello {guest}, a handyperson will visit {unit} by {fix_by} to fix the {kind} problem. Is there a time that suits you?
Hello {guest}, after your stay at {unit} we found damage: {damage}. I will send you the photos and the repair cost.
Guest: your deposit has been released
Hello {guest}, your deposit for {unit} is released. Amount returned: {returned}. Thank you for staying with us.
Guest: part of the deposit kept
Hello {guest}, we need to keep {kept_amount} of your deposit for {unit}: {reason}. I can send photos and the invoice.
Guest: thank you for reporting the issue
Hello {guest}, thank you for telling us about the {kind} problem at {unit}. It helps us look after the place.
Co-host: a ticket affects the guest
Hello, ticket {ticket_id} at {unit} affects the guest {guest}. Please keep them updated until {fix_by}.
Hello, the repair at {unit} is done (ticket {ticket_id}). The unit is ready for the next guest.
Hello, please check the lock code at {unit}. Event on {date}: {event}. Code changed: {code_changed}.
Hello, ticket {ticket_id} at {unit} ({kind}) is overdue. It was due on {fix_by}. Handyperson: {handyperson}.
Host: a damage claim is waiting
Hello, the damage claim {claim_id} of {claimed_amount} for {unit} is waiting. Days pending: {days_pending}.
Hello, the claim {claim_id} for {unit} was approved. Amount claimed {claimed_amount}. Please check the payout.
Hello, the claim {claim_id} for {unit} was rejected. Please review the evidence for the amount of {claimed_amount}.

Hello, the maintenance report for {month} at {unit} is ready: cost {cost}, cost per booked night {cost_per_night}.
Hello, the warranty of the {appliance} at {unit} ends on {warranty_until}, in {warranty_left} days. Check it for faults now.

Hello, please approve the quote of {amount} for {work} at {unit}. The supplier is {supplier}.

Hello, the maintenance costs for {month} at {unit} are attached: parts {parts_cost}, labour {labour_cost}, total {cost}.

Damage claim letter to a guest
Thank you for staying in {col:claims.unit}. After check-out we found damage: {col:claims.damage}. We took photos and kept the repair estimate. The repair cost is {col:claims.repair_cost}.

We ask for {col:claims.claimed_amount}, of which {col:claims.deposit_held} is covered by the deposit you paid. The amount still to pay is {col:claims.to_claim}. Please reply within 7 days if you want to discuss the photos or the amount.
We would like to settle this directly and fairly. Thank you for your help.
Safety check report for one check
Safety check report of {set:company}, dated {today}. Check {col:safety.safety_id} on {col:safety.date} at {col:safety.unit}.
Item: {col:safety.item}. Result: {col:safety.result}. Done by {col:safety.done_by}. Next check on {col:safety.next_check}, in {col:safety.days_left} days. Check status: {col:safety.status}.
If the result needs a repair, a ticket is opened the same day and the unit is not rented until the item is safe. Check your own local rules for the checks you must keep on record.
